evals.name: full-branch-productivity-json
evals.prompt: Analyze the dev branch of this repo and give me a productivity report as JSON.
evals.expected_output: A JSON file matching the schema in references/json-schema.md, with at least: report, headline, contributors, commit_type_breakdown, weekly_volume, weekday_distribution, hour_distribution_ist, productivity_by_area, largest_commits, commit_size_distribution_added_lines, branching_and_delivery, methodology_and_caveats.

evals.name: since-window-filter
evals.prompt: Analyze the dev branch for the last 30 days only and give me a JSON report.
evals.expected_output: JSON output where report.window reflects the filtered time range; commit count is smaller than the full-branch report.

evals.name: json-and-markdown-narrative
evals.prompt: Generate a productivity report for the dev branch — I want both the raw JSON and a Markdown summary I can send to my VP.
evals.expected_output: Two artifacts: (1) analyze-git-report.json, fully populated; (2) analyze-git-report.md with sections TL;DR, Headline, Contributors, Cadence, Productivity by area, Branching & delivery, Risks, Recommendations.

evals.name: main-branch-stale-detection
evals.prompt: Are there any release-blocking issues on this repo? Specifically, is main behind dev?
evals.expected_output: A response that surfaces branching_and_delivery.dev_ahead_of_main_commits; if it's >0, flags release blocker.

evals.name: single-author-bus-factor
evals.prompt: What's our bus factor? If one person leaves, are we screwed?
evals.expected_output: A response reading contributors[0].share_pct from the JSON; if >90%, reports bus factor = 1 and recommends pairing.
